paper: A glossary makes alias passages findable, and the gain is small: a pre-registered test of glossary attachment and citation-neighbour growth in scientific-paper retrieval
population_note: Unless a claim says otherwise, every number is over the 900 balanced records (600 G, 300 C) on 300 open-access papers of the OA-1000 corpus, questions asked with the glossary's primary term, under the served path (hybrid BM25 + dense, cross-encoder rerank, top 10). Every judged figure carries 'judge validity below threshold (prereg §13.5)'; found@10-gold is the named sensitivity. Claims in section '6x' are exploratory and decide nothing. Ids are stable; values, sources and pointers may be re-measured.

claims.statement: The balanced set holds 900 records (600 G, 300 C) on 300 papers, 2 G and 1 C each.
claims.note: records = 1,091 accepted in all; 191 of them are the held-out descriptive leg and enter no test. A point is one percentage point of records: 100/600 = 0.17 points per G record, 100/300 = 0.33 per C record, 100/900 = 0.11 per balanced record.

claims.statement: Committed code recounts the pre-registration's record table exactly: 1,091 accepted records on 408 papers, of which 600 G and 300 C form the balanced set.
claims.note: The recount compares the prereg's counts with a recomputation from the frozen record file; status 'match' on every checked figure.

claims.statement: Of the 600 G records, 508 are abbreviation aliases and 88 are symbols (4 both).
claims.note: C records: abbreviation 257, symbol 38, both 5 (same block).

claims.statement: The base corpus is 32,765 chunks of 512 tokens (SFR-Embedding-Mistral tokenizer) over 1,000 open-access papers.
claims.note: Token counts are in the Salesforce/SFR-Embedding-Mistral tokenizer (the control addendum's chunker block names it). The chunker is fixed_token/512/0 (tok512o0).

claims.statement: Every one of the 29 legs read 1,091 rows; stage A labelled 9,205 deduplicated pairs and stage B 15,354, 24,559 in all, with 0 unjudged.
claims.note: sources: 23,329 pairs by the two Qwen judges agreeing, 1,230 by the tiebreak (5.0 %). The per-leg row counts are legs_read.<leg> = 1091 on all 29 legs of the same file.

claims.statement: The merged glossary renders a field on 24,749 of 32,765 base chunks (75.5 %).
claims.note: Mean rendered length 71.2 characters per chunk (94.3 where a field is rendered). The placebo renders on 817 chunks (2.49 %), so the placebo bounds 'extra text' only at that coverage.

claims.statement: Each expanded corpus arm adds 2,423 papers to the base corpus (the citation neighbours, or a size-matched random draw).
claims.pointer: v4 expanded arms (2,423 added papers each

claims.statement: On the 600 G records under the served path, attaching the merged glossary raised judged found@10 by 1.00 point (6 records gained, 0 lost), 95 % CI [+0.33, +1.83]; H1 confirmed.
claims.note: Judge validity below threshold (prereg §13.5): the owner's spot check agreed with the final judge label on 0.872 re-weighted and 0.82 of the answers stratum, both below the frozen 0.90; found@10-gold is reported beside every judged figure. Paper-bootstrap percentile CI, 10,000 resamples. 6 non-zero papers of 300.

claims.statement: H1's exact conditional paper sign-flip p is 0.015625, which equals its minimum attainable p with 6 non-zero papers.
claims.note: One-sided at alpha 0.05. The confirmation rests on every discordant paper moving the hypothesised way.

claims.statement: G records found by some top-10 chunk under base x default: 591 of 600 without a glossary, 597 of 600 with the merged glossary, 591 of 600 with the placebo.
claims.note: Judge validity below threshold (prereg §13.5): the owner's spot check agreed with the final judge label on 0.872 re-weighted and 0.82 of the answers stratum, both below the frozen 0.90; found@10-gold is reported beside every judged figure. The baseline is 98.5 %: the G gain is measured at the ceiling.

claims.statement: On found@10-gold (the gold chunk in the top 10, no judge) the same contrast is +5.50 points.
claims.note: The sensitivity the prereg names; printed beside every judged Layer-1 figure. 37 gained, 4 lost (stage-B layer2.decisions / rr blocks).

claims.statement: The realised G discordance was 1.0 %, against planning scenarios of 5 % and 10 %.
claims.note: 6 discordant records of 600.

claims.statement: H1's power floor at the planning scenarios (q .05 / p .85 and q .10 / p .70) was .987 and .930 by the normal approximation.
claims.note: Simulation (power-v4.json) gives .99 / .92. Not read as a null: H1 was confirmed.

claims.statement: The C gate on H1 did not fire and was ceiling-limited: baseline C found@10 was 300 of 300 (100.0 %), headroom 0, and the C change under the glossary was -0.33 points (0 gained, 1 lost), 95 % CI [-1.00, 0.00].
claims.note: The gate could not have fired on a C rise however large; it is read in Layer 2 by the C-cost rule. On found@10-gold the C change is 0.00 (2 gained, 2 lost; stage-B layer2.c_change.gold_only).

claims.statement: No re-test (bootstrap-t, topic clustering) flipped H1's verdict: not fragile.
claims.note: DEVIATIONS D-1: the topic input was built after the stage-A outputs had been read; the binding figures are the first re-run with it.

claims.statement: The gain on G exceeded the change on C by 1.33 points (difference-in-differences within paper), 95 % CI [+0.50, +2.50]; 7 papers non-zero, all positive; H1b confirmed.
claims.note: Judge validity below threshold (prereg §13.5): the owner's spot check agreed with the final judge label on 0.872 re-weighted and 0.82 of the answers stratum, both below the frozen 0.90; found@10-gold is reported beside every judged figure. n = 300 papers (the unit), not 900 records. Read beside a baseline C found@10 of 100.0 % with no headroom: C could only fall or stay.

claims.statement: H1b's exact G/C label-randomization p is 0.0293, equal to its minimum attainable p.
claims.note: Fixed-sequence after H1 within Family G.

claims.statement: H1b's power floor at the planning scenarios was .67 and .54, below .80; it was confirmed, so no null is read from it.
claims.note: Simulation, C with no effect, alpha 0.05 (the artifact's own source note).

claims.statement: On found@10-gold, H1b's estimator gives +5.50 points, 95 % CI [+3.17, +7.83]; computed after the statistics ran, as a display that decides nothing (DEVIATIONS D-2).
claims.note: D-2: the committed statistics printed no gold figure beside H1b; a separate script recomputed the judged H1b exactly before writing this (h1b_judged_crosscheck.agree true). Its p is a display figure, not a test. Every sentence quoting it cites D-2.

claims.statement: On judged found@10 the neighbour arm differed from the random average by +0.06 points (11 gained, 9 lost of 900), 95 % CI [-0.72, +0.78]; H2 not confirmed.
claims.note: Judge validity below threshold (prereg §13.5): the owner's spot check agreed with the final judge label on 0.872 re-weighted and 0.82 of the answers stratum, both below the frozen 0.90; found@10-gold is reported beside every judged figure. One-sided test for a drop (neighbour < random average), default retriever, no glossary.

claims.statement: H2's exact sign-flip p is 0.615.
claims.note: Minimum attainable p 1.9e-6 with 19 non-zero papers, so the member was evaluable.

claims.statement: On found@10-gold the neighbour arm found 2.17 points fewer than the random average, 95 % CI [-3.50, -0.94]; the gold-only direction gate passes.
claims.note: 776 against 795.5 of 900 (random-1 798, random-2 793): 35 lost, 16 gained (stage-B layer2 cells and the H2 row of the other-contrasts table). Quoted first in every H2 sentence because the judged net lies within the false-yes bound.

claims.statement: The equivalence bound reads no effect larger than 1.39 points on judged found@10 (90 % CI within +-1.3863, the realised 80 %-power MDE at the realised discordance of 2.2 %).
claims.note: About 12.5 of 900 records. The planning MDE at q 5 % was 2.08 points (power-v4 mde80_points.H2).

claims.statement: H2's net lies within the random-draw gap (0.11 points) and within the judge false-yes bound B = 2.48 points.
claims.note: B = 100 x U x J_r / 900 with U the Wilson upper limit of the Opus-not share among final-answers drift pairs in the random arm (4 of 35) and J_r = 86 records resting on judged pairs only in the random cells. B never changes a label.

claims.statement: The simulated power to confirm H2 at the planning scenarios was .96 (q .05, p .85) and .90 (q .10, p .70), so a drop of the planned sizes would have been seen.
claims.note: Planned drops of 3.5 and 4.0 points at the planned dose (mu = q(2p-1)); about 3.0 and 3.5 at the realised dose 0.865. Power to confirm at a = 0.7 (the procedure, not the test alone).

claims.statement: At the realised discordance (2.2 %, between the tabulated 2 % and 3 % scenarios) the power to confirm at p .85 lay between .73 and .88, so only the equivalence bound reads smaller effects.
claims.note: Quote the power floor beside the null: H2 is a powered null for the planned drop and an unresolved contrast below about 1.4 points.

claims.statement: No re-test (bootstrap-t, topic clustering, chunk-volume covariate) flipped H2's verdict: not fragile.
claims.note: DEVIATIONS D-1 applies to the topic and volume inputs.

claims.statement: Stage A labelled 9,205 deduplicated pairs, 8,580 by the two primary judges agreeing and 625 by the tiebreak (6.8 %).
claims.note: Pairs are judged blind to arm, retriever and rank, and deduplicated across cells before labelling.

claims.statement: Exploratory: re-judging 300 stage-A pairs against a sentence- and section-bounded chunk covering the same text flipped the final label on 40 of 300 (13.3 %, Wilson [9.9, 17.7]).
claims.note: EXPLORATORY, post-freeze, judge-only control (ADDENDUM-2026-11-05); changes no confirmatory figure; no test was run or planned; Wilson 95 % intervals. Control chunk: sentence/512/0 with section cuts, ceiling 640 SFR tokens; each stage-A window mapped to the control chunk of largest character overlap.

claims.statement: Exploratory: re-judging the identical 300 stage-A windows through the identical judge path flipped 20 of 300 (6.7 %, Wilson [4.4, 10.1]): about half the control's flip rate is the judge's own non-repeatability.
claims.note: EXPLORATORY, post-freeze, judge-only control (ADDENDUM-2026-11-05); changes no confirmatory figure; no test was run or planned; Wilson 95 % intervals. Added after the control's flip rate had been seen, on owner approval. The two overall intervals overlap near 10 %, so the overall rates are not cleanly separated. Gateway temperature is the provider default and unrecorded.

claims.statement: Exploratory: on pairs both Qwen judges had called answers in stage A, the control flipped 28 of 150 to not (18.7 %) against 6 of 150 on the retest (4.0 %); on agreed not pairs 0 of 99 against 1 of 99.
claims.note: EXPLORATORY, post-freeze, judge-only control (ADDENDUM-2026-11-05); changes no confirmatory figure; no test was run or planned; Wilson 95 % intervals. Stratum and route were pre-specified but read after the overall rate; the agreed-answers contrast is the clearest pattern in this sample and confirming it would need a new pre-registered test.

claims.statement: Exploratory: on tiebroken pairs the control (12 of 51, 23.5 %) is indistinguishable from the retest (13 of 51, 25.5 %).
claims.note: EXPLORATORY, post-freeze, judge-only control (ADDENDUM-2026-11-05); changes no confirmatory figure; no test was run or planned; Wilson 95 % intervals. These pairs carry no boundary evidence in this sample; the stratum resolves nothing below about 10 %.

claims.statement: Exploratory: for 24 of the 28 agreed-route lost answers (85.7 %, Wilson [68.5, 94.3]) an overlapping control chunk answers on its own: the evidence moved to a neighbouring chunk rather than disappearing.
claims.note: EXPLORATORY, post-freeze, judge-only control (ADDENDUM-2026-11-05); changes no confirmatory figure; no test was run or planned; Wilson 95 % intervals. Cover-any judged every control chunk overlapping a flipped window (85 chunks for 40 pairs). Each 'answers' behind the count is still a judge label.

claims.statement: Exploratory: the gateway tiebreaker gave the same verdict on 27 of 34 byte-identical prompts (79.4 %, Wilson [63.2, 89.7]); escalation membership overlapped at Jaccard 0.53 between stage A and the retest.
claims.note: EXPLORATORY, post-freeze, judge-only control (ADDENDUM-2026-11-05); changes no confirmatory figure; no test was run or planned; Wilson 95 % intervals. Verdict agreement, not response identity. The escalation rate is stable (51 vs 47 of 300) while its membership churns.
